known_limitations.description: PhotoPrism is the currently cataloged runtime app; cross-app coverage grows from the same contract.

known_limitations.description: Application-owned media indexing is not a Pocket Lab parity authority.
known_limitations.label: Apps

known_limitations.description: Restore apply and update apply remain unavailable unless separately implemented and validated.
known_limitations.label: Apps

known_limitations.description: Heartbeat freshness can move during capture; comparison records the observed revision.
known_limitations.label: Devices

known_limitations.description: Per-device profile fields remain partial when the agent has not published them.
known_limitations.label: Devices

known_limitations.description: Healthy online devices are not removed without explicit confirmation.
known_limitations.label: Devices

known_limitations.description: CPU, memory, and storage presentation may be rounded or unit-formatted.
known_limitations.label: Home

known_limitations.description: Live runtime semantic evidence remains explicit and release-bound.
known_limitations.label: Home

known_limitations.description: Home never executes system operations directly.
known_limitations.label: Home

known_limitations.description: Credential values are never observable parity fields.
known_limitations.label: Identity

known_limitations.description: Identity guard and protected server-host authority fields are planned and may remain unavailable until identity bootstrap services are implemented.
known_limitations.label: Identity

known_limitations.description: The current tab is direct-rendered and has no dedicated selector layer.
known_limitations.label: Identity

known_limitations.description: Identity guard and protected server-host projections are not fully implemented.
known_limitations.label: Identity

known_limitations.description: Identity mismatch repair/rejoin must remain explicit and fail closed.
known_limitations.label: Identity

known_limitations.description: Status labels intentionally use Lite-friendly wording instead of raw backend enums.
known_limitations.label: Backup & Restore

known_limitations.description: App restore apply remains explicitly unsupported where the repository reports it unavailable.
known_limitations.label: Backup & Restore

known_limitations.description: Historical restore previews are evidence only and never authorize a new restore.
known_limitations.label: Backup & Restore

known_limitations.description: Live Termux and live browser semantic capture remain explicit; missing capture is not drift.
known_limitations.label: Backup & Restore

known_limitations.description: Unsafe writes remain disabled while the recovery projection is stale.
known_limitations.label: Backup & Restore

known_limitations.description: The current product contract is a protection-mode policy surface, not a general arbitrary rule engine.

security_controls.description: Frontend does not connect directly to NATS.
failure_consequences: browser could bypass the control API and attempt unauthorized messaging/command injection

security_controls.description: Frontend does not execute shell commands.
failure_consequences: browser-originated input could reach host shell execution and mutate the server host

security_controls.description: FastAPI remains the frontend-facing control API.
failure_consequences: frontend intent could bypass centralized validation, authorization, reason codes and audit ownership

security_controls.description: Human browser writes require an authenticated local-owner session plus a separate same-site CSRF proof; session credentials remain HttpOnly and hash-only at rest.
failure_consequences: ambient browser session authority could be reused without a separate write-intent proof or reusable session material could be exposed

security_controls.description: FastAPI preserves hard domain invariants, then requires a valid loopback OPA allow decision for registered protected actions before NATS/worker execution; unavailable, timed-out, malformed, or unregistered decisions fail closed.
failure_consequences: a protected mutation could proceed without a valid authorization decision or while policy state is unavailable or ambiguous

security_controls.description: Workers, agents and supervisors own execution and recovery.
failure_consequences: commands or recovery could execute outside worker/agent/supervisor ownership and lose delivery/recovery guarantees

security_controls.description: Runtime/scanner evidence is sanitized before canonical documentation ingestion.
failure_consequences: secret-bearing or private-path evidence could enter canonical documentation or mislead security posture

security_controls.description: Runtime and scanner evidence promotion is explicit; MkDocs does not capture or promote.
failure_consequences: transient/unreviewed capture could be mistaken for canonical release/runtime evidence

security_controls.description: Pinned WSL2/CI tooling produces sanitized normalized SBOM/security evidence before docs consumption.
failure_consequences: unqualified dependencies or release artifacts could enter runtime without normalized SBOM/scanner evidence

supply_chain.termux_policy: bounded existing runtime evidence only; no whole-filesystem SBOM or heavy scanning from docs generation

tools.execution_surface: WSL2/CI and bounded existing Termux profiles

Secondary SBOM vulnerability corroboration without treating scanner disagreement as automatic failure

tools.purpose: Community static analysis plus Pocket Lab architecture-boundary rules

tools.platform: WSL2/Ubuntu Linux amd64/arm64 via isolated pinned PyPI virtualenv

consequences_without_model: Trust assumptions become implicit and easier to violate during change.
Controls can exist without a clear statement of which threats and assets they protect.
Runtime, release and supply-chain evidence become disconnected from security reasoning.
Boundary changes can ship without exposing their security-review impact.
Duplicated, missing or weakly evidenced controls are harder to identify.
Residual risk and human-review decisions become less auditable.

controls.description: Frontend does not connect directly to NATS.
failure_consequences: browser could bypass the control API and attempt unauthorized messaging/command injection

controls.description: Frontend does not execute shell commands.
failure_consequences: browser-originated input could reach host shell execution and mutate the server host

controls.description: FastAPI remains the frontend-facing control API.
failure_consequences: frontend intent could bypass centralized validation, authorization, reason codes and audit ownership

controls.description: Human browser writes require an authenticated local-owner session plus a separate same-site CSRF proof; session credentials remain HttpOnly and hash-only at rest.
failure_consequences: ambient browser session authority could be reused without a separate write-intent proof or reusable session material could be exposed

controls.description: FastAPI preserves hard domain invariants, then requires a valid loopback OPA allow decision for registered protected actions before NATS/worker execution; unavailable, timed-out, malformed, or unregistered decisions fail closed.
failure_consequences: a protected mutation could proceed without a valid authorization decision or while policy state is unavailable or ambiguous

controls.description: Workers, agents and supervisors own execution and recovery.
failure_consequences: commands or recovery could execute outside worker/agent/supervisor ownership and lose delivery/recovery guarantees

controls.description: Runtime/scanner evidence is sanitized before canonical documentation ingestion.
failure_consequences: secret-bearing or private-path evidence could enter canonical documentation or mislead security posture

controls.description: Runtime and scanner evidence promotion is explicit; MkDocs does not capture or promote.
failure_consequences: transient/unreviewed capture could be mistaken for canonical release/runtime evidence

controls.description: Pinned WSL2/CI tooling produces sanitized normalized SBOM/security evidence before docs consumption.
failure_consequences: unqualified dependencies or release artifacts could enter runtime without normalized SBOM/scanner evidence

exclusions: Live attack monitoring or packet inspection
Live NATS polling or traffic visualization
Running Trivy, Lynis, Semgrep or other scanners from MkDocs
Scanning the live Android filesystem from documentation generation
Automatically deciding whether a vulnerability is exploitable
Automatically accepting residual risk or security exceptions
Replacing penetration testing, source review or operational monitoring
Replacing incident detection, release qualification or runtime health checks

application: Identify canonical trust boundaries, assets, actors and flows.
Generate STRIDE candidates for every trust boundary.
Map repository-owned controls to applicable threat categories and boundaries.
Attach promoted runtime, security, release and dependency evidence to control posture.
Require human review for threat relevance, mitigation adequacy, residual risk, risk acceptance and exceptions.

definitions.Denial of Service: Loss of availability, command delivery or recovery capability.
definitions.Elevation of Privilege: Bypassing browser, control API, execution-owner or host boundaries.
definitions.Information Disclosure: Exposure of secrets, private paths, credentials or sensitive operational metadata.
definitions.Repudiation: Loss of trustworthy evidence about who or what performed an action.
definitions.Spoofing: Impersonating a user, device, service or release identity.
definitions.Tampering: Unauthorized modification of commands, durable state, releases or evidence.

threat_model.posture_rule: derived only from canonical source plus promoted sanitized runtime/security/release/dependency evidence; never live monitoring
